data.plain: Writes, release steps, releasing a claim on a path, source imports and anything that can be rolled back need evidence that their steps ran in order as one transaction. Release a lock only after the durable records are written, recompute after the release, and block a change whose parent commit is stale or whose path someone else has claimed.

analogy.boundary: The transfer picture covers one transaction only; one clean transfer tells you nothing about the rest of the bank.

maps.analogy: the transfer being treated as sent
maps.doctrine: the effect being treated as done

maps.analogy: the entry in the bank's ledger
a reversal path, or a stated point after which it cannot be pulled back
maps.doctrine: a way to undo it, or a declared point of no return

maps.analogy: confirming the balance is still the one the clerk started from
no second clerk touching the same account at the same moment

analogy.text: A bank transfer counts as sent once the bank writes it into its ledger, attaches a way to reverse it, and confirms no other clerk changed the same account at the same moment from an out-of-date balance.

reader.counterexample: A release step reports success after taking a lock and before writing the lasting record, so a crash in between leaves an effect that looks done with nothing to recompute or undo.
reader.does_not_prove: Guarding one transaction on one path says nothing about effects that never went through that guard.

example.text: The mission transaction work spine marks a multi-step change done only after the lasting record is written, recomputes once the lock is released, and blocks a stale parent or a conflict on the same path, so a half-applied write cannot be reported as complete.

reader.governs: The point where an operation is about to be treated as done.
reader.plain: An action counts as done only when there is a permanent record of it, a way to undo it or a stated point of no return, and a check that nobody else changed the same thing at the same time from outdated information. Running without errors is not enough.
reader.potential_misread: That an operation which reported success must be fully done, when the risky moment is the gap where a lock is released before the permanent record exists.
reader.refuses: Counting an operation as done when the lock was released before the record was written, the parent is stale, or a second writer is on the same path.
reader.requires: An ordered lasting record, a way to undo it or a declared irreversible point, a compare-and-swap on the expected parent, and one writer holding the path.
reader.why_it_matters: A step that crashes between starting and finishing could otherwise look complete while leaving a half-done change nobody can recompute or undo.
